metadata.title: इंद्रावती जंगल में धवस्त होता माओवादी गढ़ | The Crumbling Maoist Stronghold in Indravati Forest
metadata.description:
In the dense forests of Chhattisgarh's Bastar region, the conflict between security forces and Maoists continues to intensify. As part of their anti-Maoist operations, security forces are mounting pressure through sustained encounters and combing operations, especially in areas like the Indravati Tiger Reserve — a known Maoist stronghold. However, these offensives have drawn serious allegations of human rights violations, with reports of atrocities being committed against innocent tribal villagers.

At the same time, Maoists are accused of unleashing brutal violence on tribal people, often targeting them on mere suspicion of being police informers. Caught in the crossfire of this prolonged war are the region's Adivasi communities, who face daily fear, displacement, and trauma.

Main Bhi Bharat Editor Shyam Sunder undertook a courageous journey through the Indravati forest on motorcycles, speaking directly with tribal families living under siege. This ground report sheds light on their untold suffering, the complex realities of the conflict, and the urgent need to protect the rights and lives of India's most vulnerable citizens.
